patient.name: Derek Simmons
patient.chiefComplaint: Unhelmeted motorcycle crash with head trauma

history.hpi: 35-year-old male lost control of his motorcycle on a curve and was ejected without a helmet, striking his head directly on the pavement. Bystanders report a brief loss of consciousness followed by confusion and repetitive questioning. He vomited once at the scene and has become progressively harder to arouse since bystanders called 911.
history.lastOralIntake: Lunch approximately 3 hours prior to the crash
history.events: High-speed loss of control on a roadway curve; patient ejected from the motorcycle without a helmet and landed in the roadside ditch

scene.dispatch: 35-year-old male, motorcycle crash, unknown responsiveness, roadway
scene.location: Rural two-lane highway curve; patient found approximately 20 feet from the motorcycle in the roadside ditch
scene.safety: Traffic control established by law enforcement; motorcycle fuel leak contained
scene.bystanders: Two witnesses report the patient was not wearing a helmet and struck his head directly on the pavement before sliding into the ditch
visualCues: Deep scalp laceration to right parietal region with active oozing
Motorcycle heavily damaged approximately 20 feet away
Patient confused and combative on initial approach
Abrasions to right shoulder and forearm

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 35-year-old male ejected from his motorcycle without a helmet, lying in the roadside ditch. He is confused, repeating the same questions, and combative with examination, with an actively oozing scalp laceration.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, speaking though confused and combative
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong and regular, skin warm and dry
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all four extremities spontaneously, combative with exam
otherFindings: Active oozing scalp laceration to right parietal region
Repeatedly asks the same questions (anterograde amnesia)
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Where... where am I? What happened?" (repeats the question)

transitions.condition: Crew maintains cervical stabilization, completes a MARCH primary survey, and applies high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather as a precaution against unanticipated deterioration, with frequent neurologic reassessment.

phases.name: Primary survey and O2 given
phases.description: Crew completes a MARCH primary survey with cervical stabilization maintained, applies high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather mask, and begins trending neurologic status given the mechanism and moderate head injury presentation.
phases.triggerCondition: After scene arrival, the crew maintains cervical stabilization, completes the primary survey per General Trauma Management, and applies high-flow oxygen as a precaution against unanticipated deterioration, continuing serial neurologic status assessments.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong and regular, skin warm and dry
otherFindings: Scalp laceration dressed with direct pressure
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Where... where am I? What happened?" (repeats the question)

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain cervical stabilization while performing MARCH primary survey
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Maintain cervical stabilization Primary survey per the General Trauma Management Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: Assume concomitant cervical spine injury with any moderate/severe head injury while ruling out other life threats.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply high-flow O2 via non-rebreather as precaution against deterioration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer high-flow oxygen via NRB (non-rebreather) as a precaution against unanticipated deterioration
expectedActions.rationale: Preoxygenation protects against unanticipated neurologic or respiratory deterioration.

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform serial GCS/AVPU checks; reassess pupils with any change in mentation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Perform and trend neurologic status assessment (GCS or AVPU scale) Reassess pupils if decrease in mentation
expectedActions.rationale: Trending neuro status is the earliest way to catch rising ICP before overt Cushing's triad develops.

transitions.condition: Serial reassessment detects GCS decline, anisocoria, hypertension, bradycardia, and irregular respirations consistent with rising ICP, prompting RSI for airway protection.

phases.name: Cushing's triad recognized, RSI performed
phases.description: The patient's GCS declines to 6 with a dilating, sluggish right pupil, rising blood pressure to 172/98, falling heart rate to 46, and irregular respirations — Cushing's triad indicating rising intracranial pressure. He can no longer protect his airway, meeting criteria for RSI with head-injury-specific ventilation targets.
phases.triggerCondition: GCS declines to 6 (P on AVPU) with anisocoria, hypertension, bradycardia, and an irregular respiratory pattern consistent with Cushing's triad from rising intracranial pressure; the patient can no longer protect his airway.

clinicalPresentation.pupils: Right pupil 6mm and sluggish, left pupil 3mm and reactive (anisocoria)

expectedActions.shortAction: Preoxygenate with high-flow O2/BVM for at least 2 minutes prior to RSI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient should be pre-oxygenated with high flow oxygen, and positive pressure ventilation for a minimum of two minutes prior to the procedure
expectedActions.rationale: Adequate preoxygenation limits peri-intubation hypoxia, especially critical in a head-injured patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 86 mcg IV pretreatment (86 kg × 1 mcg/kg), 2-3 min before intubation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider pre-medication with Fentanyl, 1 mcg/kg, 2-3 minutes prior to intubation attempt
expectedActions.rationale: Blunts the sympathetic/ICP response to laryngoscopy.

expectedActions.shortAction: Etomidate 21.5 mg IV induction (86 kg × 0.25 mg/kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Etomidate IV push, 0.2-0.3 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Etomidate provides hemodynamic stability appropriate for a head-injured patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rocuronium 86 mg IV paralytic (86 kg × 1 mg/kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer paralytic agent: Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Provides paralysis for first-pass intubation success.

expectedActions.shortAction: Intubate with 8.0 ETT; confirm placement with waveform capnography
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.rationale: Waveform capnography is the most reliable confirmation method and is required for ongoing EtCO2-guided ventilation.

transitions.if: Tube confirmed, ventilated per head-injury targets
transitions.condition: Successful intubation is confirmed with waveform capnography and secured; ventilation and fluids are titrated to head-injury-specific targets during transport.
Crew proceeds directly to sedation and paralysis without the minimum two-minute preoxygenation period, and the patient desaturates rapidly during the intubation attempt.

phases.name: Tube confirmed, ventilated per head-injury targets
phases.description: The endotracheal tube is confirmed with waveform capnography and secured. Ventilation is titrated to avoid hyperventilation and hypocapnia, and fluids are given to maintain blood pressure above the head-injury threshold while transporting to the highest level trauma center.
phases.triggerCondition: After successful intubation, the tube is confirmed with waveform capnography and secured. Ventilation is targeted to EtCO2 35-45 mmHg at 10 breaths/min, and IV fluids are given to maintain SBP ≥110 mmHg while transporting to the highest level trauma center.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured ETT confirmed with waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Strong pulses, improving blood pressure trend
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Right pupil remains 5mm and sluggish, left 3mm and reactive; being trended
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sedated and paralyzed, no spontaneous movement
otherFindings: ETT secured at 22cm at the teeth
EtCO2 waveform confirms placement, trending 38-40 mmHg
SBP maintained above 110 mmHg with fluid bolus

expectedActions.shortAction: Ventilate at 10 breaths/min targeting EtCO2 35-45 mmHg; avoid hyperventilation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Do not hyperventilate patients: Maintain all patients in EtCO2 range of 35–45 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Hyperventilation causes cerebral vasoconstriction, worsening secondary brain injury.

expectedActions.shortAction: NS bolus to maintain SBP ≥110 mmHg; do not wait for hypotension to develop
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Adult (age greater than 10 years): maintain SBP greater than or equal to 110 mmHg Administer normal saline (NS)/lactated Ringer's (LR) fluid boluses to maintain SBP above threshold. Do not wait until after the patient is already hypotensive—prevent hypotension
expectedActions.rationale: Preventing hypotension avoids further cerebral hypoperfusion and secondary brain injury.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to highest level trauma center per severe head injury criteria
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Preferential transport to highest level of care within trauma system: GCS 3–13, P (pain) or U (unresponsive) on AVPU scale
expectedActions.rationale: Severe TBI requires neurosurgical capability at the receiving facility.

phases.name: RSI without pre-O2
phases.description: Crew proceeds directly to sedation and paralysis without the minimum two-minute preoxygenation period. The patient desaturates rapidly during the intubation attempt, developing hypoxic bradycardia.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew skips adequate preoxygenation before administering sedation and paralytics, and the patient desaturates rapidly during the intubation attempt.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Intubation attempt in progress, tube not yet placed
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Apneic (paralyzed), no ventilation ongoing during the attempt
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Right pupil 6mm and sluggish, left 3mm and reactive

expectedActions.shortAction: Stop the intubation attempt; resume BVM with high-flow O2 to recover SpO2 before re-attempting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Attempt intubation, limiting attempts to 15 seconds, or a desaturation below 90%, whichever occurs first
expectedActions.rationale: Continuing an attempt through severe desaturation risks hypoxic cardiac arrest.
